questions: Did the facial asymmetry begin suddenly, within the last 72 hours?
Is the weakness present on the same side of the forehead, eyelid, and mouth?
Have you had difficulty closing the affected eye completely?
Have you noticed decreased taste on the affected side?
Have you had ear pain, hearing loss, dizziness, or blisters/rash around the ear?
Do you have weakness or numbness in an arm or leg, trouble speaking, or severe headache?
Has one upper eyelid been drooping for months or years rather than recently?
Is the pupil on the drooping-eyelid side smaller than the other pupil?
Does the difference in pupil size or eyelid droop become more noticeable in dim light?
Do you have double vision or difficulty moving either eye in any direction?
Does the drooping eyelid improve or worsen after prolonged use, such as later in the day?
Have you ever had injury or surgery involving the eye, face, neck, or chest?
Is the double vision present only when both eyes are open and absent when either eye is covered?
Is the double vision worse when looking up, down, or toward one particular side?
Does the affected eye appear pushed forward or bulge compared with the other eye?
Do you have eye pain, pain with eye movement, redness, or reduced vision?
Have you had symptoms of an overactive thyroid, such as weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, or rapid heartbeat?
Is the affected eye unable to move outward fully?
Have you had fever, severe headache, facial pain, nasal congestion, or purulent nasal discharge?
Do you have diabetes, poorly controlled blood sugar, or a weakened immune system?
Have you recently had COVID-19, another serious infection, or treatment with corticosteroids?
Did the eye pain and vision/eye-movement problem worsen rapidly over hours to days?
Have you had black discoloration or tissue damage inside the nose or on the palate?
orders: Bedside visual-acuity testing in each eye separately, with current glasses or contact lenses if normally used
Bedside pupillary examination, including direct and consensual responses and assessment for a relative afferent pupillary defect
Formal extraocular-movement examination, documenting pain, limitation, and nystagmus in each direction of gaze
Slit-lamp examination of the painful eye with fluorescein staining and Seidel test
Dilated fundus examination of both eyes
Urgent MRI of the brain and orbits with and without gadolinium contrast, including thin cuts through the brainstem, optic nerves, cavernous sinuses, and orbital apex
Magnetic-resonance angiography of the head and neck
Optical coherence tomography of both optic nerves and maculae
Automated visual fields for each eye separately
Blood tests for CBC, ESR, CRP, ANA, ACE, aquaporin-4 IgG, and MOG-IgG
Serum Lyme antibody testing and syphilis serology (RPR/VDRL with treponemal confirmation)
Urgent contrast-enhanced CT of the paranasal sinuses and facial bones, assessing for sinus opacification, bony destruction, and orbital-apex involvement
Urgent ENT nasal endoscopy with direct inspection of the nasal cavity and palate
Endoscopic biopsy of any abnormal sinonasal or orbital-apex tissue for histopathology, fungal stains, bacterial and fungal cultures
Serum glucose, HbA1c, renal function, and serum beta-D-glucan and galactomannan levels
served: fungal culture / KOH of nasal tissue
